promptState.text: A cute cartoon 3D render of a fluffy white bunny in a Pixar-like style, a close-up portrait from the chest up. It has big shiny dark eyes, rosy cheeks and a small happy smile, and wears an orange hoodie with the word "PIXA" printed in white on the chest. Warm window light from the left, a cozy room softly blurred behind, shallow depth of field.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt.
  • Load VAE - Turns the finished render into a picture. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can make transparent pictures.

 The speed node

Teal, above the graph.

  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. The note on the right has the numbers. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Pick Orientation and Size - The size of the picture. The starred sizes are the native 2K sizes Qwen lists for this model; the others are smaller and much faster. For video, 1920 x 1088 is Full HD (the model works in steps of 16 pixels, so 1080 becomes 1088) and 2560 x 1440 is 1440p. The orientation switch flips a size between portrait and landscape.
  • 2. Add a prompt - What you want to see. Put any words you want written in the picture in quotes, like the word on the hoodie in the demo prompt.
  • 3. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same picture, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt through the text encoder. It has a negative prompt box, but that does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas, at the size from step 1.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template. The note on the right says what 40 steps costs.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the picture and saves it to your output folder as a PNG. PNG keeps transparency, so a transparent picture stays transparent.

The dark Run Timer above it shows how long the last Run took. Handy when you are trying sizes against the table in the other note.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

A picture from a prompt, with Qwen Image 2.1. It renders natively at 2K, and it writes text well: put the words you want in quotes. In all 18 test renders made for this note, the word on the hoodie in the demo prompt came out spelled right.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

SizePixels25 steps
1024 x 1024about 1 MP5 s
1152 x 864about 1 MP5 s
1248 x 832about 1 MP5 s
1376 x 768about 1 MP5 s
1920 x 1088Full HD, about 2.1 MP10 s
1536 x 1536about 2.4 MP12 s
2560 x 14401440p, about 3.7 MP21 s
2048 x 2048native 2K, 4.2 MP26 s
2400 x 1792native 2K, 4.3 MP27 s
2528 x 1696native 2K, 4.3 MP27 s
2752 x 1536native 2K, 4.2 MP26 s

The table lists the sizes landscape. This workflow opens in portrait, where each size is simply turned on its side (832 x 1248 and so on), and turning a size does not change the time: 5 s for 864 x 1152 against 5 s for 1152 x 864, and 26 s for 1536 x 2752 against 26 s for 2752 x 1536.

The picture's size is what costs you: 2048 x 2048 has four times the pixels of 1024 x 1024 and took about five times as long. Work out your prompt at a 1 MP size, then switch to a starred size for the picture you keep.

 Video sizes: Full HD and 1440p

Full HD is 1920 x 1088 here. The model works in steps of 16 pixels, so 1080 is not possible: asking for 1920 x 1080 gives exactly the same 1920 x 1088 picture. For an exact 1920 x 1080, trim 8 pixels off the top or the bottom. 1440p, 2560 x 1440, divides evenly and comes out exact. In portrait they are 1088 x 1920 and 1440 x 2560, for vertical video.

 Steps: 25 or 40

This workflow uses 25 steps, the setting from ComfyUI's own template. Qwen's own example code uses 40, which takes about half as long again on the same seed:

Size25 steps40 steps
1024 x 10245 s7 s
1536 x 153612 s19 s
2048 x 204826 s40 s

On the same seed the 40-step pictures came out almost the same as the 25-step ones, not clearly better, so 25 stays. To try 40, change steps on the KSampler.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 2048 x 2048, it took 26 s, against 39 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out practically the same. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder. Measured on a 1024 x 1024 picture: 8 s with the models unloaded first, 5 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 23 GB during these runs, at 2048 x 2048. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 Transparent pictures

Qwen Image 2.1 can make a picture with a transparent background. Start and end your prompt with Qwen's own wording and put your subject in the middle:

This is an RGBA image with transparency. [your subject]. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.

Preview Image Pixaroma saves a PNG, which keeps the transparency; in the preview the transparent part shows the node's own dark grey. Under the transparent part the picture is a flat purple. You never see it in a PNG, but anything that throws the transparency away, like saving as JPG, will show it.

Every picture from this model carries a transparency channel, even a normal one. On a normal picture it is almost fully opaque (252 to 255 out of 255), so you will not see it, but an image editor will open the PNG as a layer with transparency.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 810, "height": 1791, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}
